summary: Tashi Densapa worked in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He served as editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology (attested 1978, 2002) and as director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (attested 2008).

Specializing in Tibetology, history/archaeology, and linguistics, he studied at the Central School for Tibetans and under numerous teachers including Tenzin Gyatso. He held posts at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (~1979–1995) and CIHTS (attested 2005, 2014–2019).

Tatiana Oranskaia works in Indology and linguistics. She studied at the University of Saint Petersburg (~1967–1972) and Kendriya Hindi Sansthan (~1987–1988), later holding positions at Saint Petersburg (1973–1998) and the University of Hamburg (1995–1996, 1998–2016).

Tatsugen Sato worked in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his doctorate at Komazawa University by 1978, where he served as an associate professor (~1968–1995) and professor (~1978–1995), alongside lectureships at Ryukoku and Tokai universities.
Working in Buddhist studies, Tatsuhiro Saito studied under Kenyu Mitomo (attested 1996) and founded Buha Bukkyo Shiso Kenkyukai.

Tatsuo Hayashi specialized in philosophy and history/archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1917–1921) and held posts at Hosei University (~1925–1932), Toyo University (~1928–1932), Tsuda University (~1938–1957), Meiji University, and Rikkyo University.

A scholar of linguistics, Tibetology, and sinology, he earned his doctorate at Kyoto University in 1962. His main career was at Kyoto University (1956–1992, professor from 1972), followed by the National Center for Science Information Systems (1992–1994).

Tatyana Elizarenkova was an Indologist and linguist. She studied under Mikhaïl Peterson at the Philological Faculty of Moscow State University (~1946–1951) and held a post at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1957–2007).

Working in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, he earned an M.A. at the University of Hawaiʻi and studied under Luangpor Teean Jittasubho in 1980. He held posts at Kyoto University, Mahidol University (attested 2005), and World Buddhist University (attested 2013).
Taw Sein Ko worked in history/archaeology and sinology. He studied at the University of Rangoon and subsequently at the Inner Temple and Inns of Court (~1892–1893).

Teizo Iyanaga specialized in history/archaeology and Japanology. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1935–1938), he held posts at Nagoya University (~1949–1950), the University of Tokyo (~1950–1976), and Sophia University (~1976–1983).
Tej Ram Sharma specialized in history/archaeology and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Banaras Hindu University (~1964–1968) and held a post at Himachal Pradesh University (~1971).
Tendzin Chökyi Gyatso studied under Tenzin Gyatso and Lobsang Gyatso, and also taught Lobsang Gyatso.
Tenga Rinpoche was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Benchen Monastery under Situ Rinpoche and served as Dorje Lopön at Rumtek Monastery (~1967–1984).

A scholar of Buddhist studies, he studied at Ryukoku University until 1955 and served there as lecturer, professor (from 1970), and president (1995–1999). He later served as president of Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University (1999–2005).
Tenshin Tanouye was active in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied under Sogen Omori and founded Chozen-ji.
Tenzin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed a Master of Philosophy at the University of Oslo under supervisor Hanna Havnevik (attested 2008).

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he studied under Geshe Lobsang Tsephel, Geshe Sonam Rinchen, and Geshe Dawa. He worked as a translator at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives and at Pullahari Monastery (attested 2000).

Working in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, he studied under Trijang Rinpoche, Ling Rinpoche, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, Dilgo Khyentse, and Trulshik Rinpoche, among others, and founded the International Network of Engaged Buddhists in 1989.

A scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies, he studied under traditional teachers Reting Rinpoche, Taktra Rinpoche, Ling Rinpoche, and Trijang Rinpoche, and taught Jeffrey Hopkins, Robert A. F. Thurman, and James B. Apple.
